artifactText: {"schemaVersion":1,"findings":[{"id":"sql-injection-in-invoice-query","title":"Customer input is interpolated into SQL","severity":"critical","location":"Lines 8-10 in the /invoice handler.","evidence":"Line 9 constructs SQL with `customer = '${req.query.customer}'`, and line 10 passes that constructed string to `db.query(sql)` without parameter binding.","repair":"Use the database driver's parameterized-query API, for example `db.query('SELECT id, total FROM invoices WHERE customer = ?', [req.query.customer])`, and validate the customer identifier against the expected format.","confidence":"high"},{"id":"path-traversal-in-download-route","title":"Requested download name can traverse outside the data directory","severity":"high","location":"Lines 14-16 in the /download handler.","evidence":"Line 15 joins request-controlled `req.query.name` with `DATA_ROOT`; traversal components such as `../` are normalized by `path.join`, and no containment check verifies the resulting path remains inside `/srv/app/downloads`.","repair":"Resolve both the root and candidate path with `path.resolve`, reject candidates outside the resolved root plus separator, and preferably map an allowlisted file identifier to a server-controlled filename.","confidence":"high"},{"id":"command-injection-in-diagnostics","title":"Host input is interpolated into a shell command","severity":"critical","location":"Lines 19-23 in the /diagnostics handler, especially line 20.","evidence":"Line 20 passes a template literal containing `req.body.host` to `exec`, which invokes a shell. Shell metacharacters in the request value can alter the command executed.","repair":"Replace `exec` with `execFile` or `spawn` using a fixed executable and argument array, such as `execFile('ping', ['-c', '1', validatedHost], callback)`, and strictly validate the host as an IP address or constrained hostname.","confidence":"high"}],"summary":"The supplied routes directly place request-controlled values into SQL, a filesystem path, and a shell command, creating SQL injection, path traversal, and command injection exposure."}
